lesson: [lfm2.5_vl_450m] Weight reading found clean month-name output units, but they were not the causal bottleneck. L13 unit 4374 (cosine .50 to the mean month direction) and L15 unit 3041 (.48) had negative logit-lens top-10s made up entirely of month names. Yet ablating 4 L15 units moved month_successor by -.011, and 4 L13 units moved it by only .064.

[lfm2.5_vl_450m] Attribution on the layer just before the month writer found the real part. L12 units 1322, 1189 and 1069 dropped month_successor by .658 against a number-successor control of .027, and passed the screen (random same-size parts: at most .013). Recipe: use weights to find the output writer, then run attribution_scan one layer upstream.

[lfm2.5_vl_450m] Trimming a part to its top attribution units fixed leaky controls. The 7-unit L12 attribution set dropped the target by .791 but the control by .262, which is borderline failing. The top 3 alone kept a .658 drop with the control at .027.

[lfm2.5_vl_450m] A clean search-split result can still fail the held-out check. 5 L13 month-writer units dropped the target by .199 with control .007 and built-ins at most .002, but failed held-out. Growing the cluster to 13 weight-ranked units did not help (.183). Aim for a search drop well above .15 (for example above .3) before spending a screen.

[lfm2.5_vl_450m] Untested weight leads for future runs: colour writers at L13 unit 515 (cosine .46) and L15 unit 3863 (.50); digit writers at L15 units 2699 (-.59) and 2946 (.52) and L14 unit 2734 (-.47). Following lesson 2, try attribution one layer upstream of these. Sandbox variables do not persist between run_python calls, so redefine P, U and the other helpers in every call.

[lfm2.5_vl_450m] Growing a causal seed into its weight family produced large parts that passed. Rank units by |cos| of the w1 gate row plus |cos| of the w2 output column against the seeds. Families passed at 64 to 1024 units: antonym L8 at 1024 dropped .737, pronoun L14 at 1024 dropped .696, weekday L13 at 1024 dropped .489. Random same-size parts mostly dropped the target by less than .15, with a few up to .2-.44. Seed neighbourhoods with a 16th-neighbour score around .3-.8 (vs a ~.1 background) predicted a real family.

[lfm2.5_vl_450m] Subtracting hub units fixed leaky large families. Hubs are units that recur in 3 or more of your families in the same layer (L14: 1364, 722; L15: 241, 1475, 3878). Penalise similarity to them and to other skills' seeds. Examples: L14 pronoun went from .17 with facts leaking .25 to .642; L14 past tense at 512 units went from .21 with facts .14 to .415; L11 comparative at 256 went from a .434 month leak to .65 clean.

[lfm2.5_vl_450m] Math, code and facts did not localise into MLP families, head groups or blocks. Logit-lens digit writers (z up to 6) and digit-input detectors (selectivity ratio 22x) moved math by at most .01 even at 128 units. Code and facts families reached at most .05-.06. Every single-layer block ablation dropped several skills by .3-.9. L12 head 15 dropped math .49, but it is a copy head: it also dropped month .79 and month's copy control .63.

[lfm2.5_vl_450m] Head groups are risky in attention layers where random head sets are destructive. L8 heads 4-7 for antonym (.687) failed because a random 4-head set dropped antonym .90. L12 heads [1,2,3,12] for pronoun (.824) failed against a random .92. Groups that passed were contiguous GQA quads in less fragile spots: L5 heads 12-15 for month (.846), L14 heads 10-13 for comparative (.47), L2 heads [2,3,9,12,15] for multilingual (.519).

[lfm2.5_vl_450m] Month parts often fail the held-out check, so prefer high search drops and early layers. L13 (.294), L9 (.253) and L10 (.193) month families all failed held-out. The L8 family seeded on attribution units 4251, 293, 1022 with antonym and comparative subtracted passed at 64, 256 and 512 units (.635-.736). Antonym-seeded L9/L12 families dropped month more than antonym, so subtract month units from antonym families.
